name: Work health and safety
what: Manage risks to workers and others, consult workers, keep records, report incidents and hold high-risk work licences where needed.

layers.who: State work health and safety law
State work health and safety regulator

consistency_note: Model laws adopted state by state, with variations. When the Productivity Commission reported in 2016, Victoria and Western Australia had not adopted them.

basis.quote: All jurisdictions except Victoria and Western Australia have adopted the model WHS laws.

issues.what: The model WHS laws are in force everywhere except Victoria, which keeps its own OHS law, and adopting states have made their own variations.

evidence.source: 5-year Productivity Inquiry: A more productive labour market (volume 7)
evidence.quote: Model WHS laws, which are implemented in all states and territories bar Victoria

the lack of harmonisation across state and territory workplace safety frameworks, particularly with respect to workers compensation, increases compliance costs and administrative complexity for companies operating across borders

issues.status_note: Every state and territory except Victoria has implemented the model laws (PC 2023).

issues.what: A business can deal with more than one safety regulator: a state regulator and Comcare on mixed sites, or separate regulators for mining, electrical safety or dangerous goods.

evidence.source: Performance Benchmarking of Australian Business Regulation: Occupational Health and Safety
evidence.quote: In addition, a business may have to interact with more than one regulator, either within or across jurisdictions. Different approaches to enforcement by these regulators could also create additional burdens.
